parsed.use_case: A batch-processing service must choose the slowest worker rate that still clears a known queue before a deadline, where each job occupies a worker for at least one time unit and partial work on a job cannot be carried across time slots. Picking the minimum sufficient rate avoids overprovisioning while meeting the service-level deadline.
system_examples: Batch processing systems — sizing per-worker throughput to finish a fixed set of indivisible jobs before a deadline, with at most one job assigned per worker per interval.
parsed.explanation: The feasibility of a candidate rate is monotonic, so binary search finds the minimum valid rate while summing the required time across piles. This takes O(n log M) time for n piles and maximum pile size M, instead of checking each possible rate in O(nM); it is useful when deadline constraints must be met without excessive capacity.
